You are going to investigate the rate of reaction between hydrochloric acid and aqueous sodium
thiosulfate. When these chemicals react they form a precipitate which makes the solution go cloudy.
The formation of this precipitate can be used to show how fast the reaction proceeds.
Read all the instructions below carefully before starting the experiments.
Instructions
You are going to carry out ﬁ ve experiments using the apparatus shown below.

250cm3 conical flask
aqueous sodium thiosulfate

printed text

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Experiment 1
Use the large measuring cylinder to pour 50 cm3 of aqueous sodium thiosulfate into a conical
ﬂ ask. Place the conical ﬂ ask on the printed insert provided.
Fill the small measuring cylinder with 10 cm3 of the hydrochloric acid provided.
Add the acid to the solution in the conical ﬂ ask and immediately start your timer and swirl the
mixture.
Measure the time taken for the printed text to disappear from view. Record the time in the table.
Pour the solution away and rinse the conical ﬂ ask with distilled water.
